'Not talking this week': Fitzgibbon out to turn tables on former mentor
Craig Fitzgibbon has opened up on the key role Trent Robinson played in his development as a coach as he looks to turn the tables on his former mentor.
The pair will go head-to-head when the Sharks take on the Roosters in Saturday's sudden-death semi-final at Allianz Stadium.
A premiership winner with the Roosters as a player, Fitzgibbon transitioned to coaching soon after hanging up the boots and was a key member of Robinson's coaching staff for a decade.
Fitzgibbon gets another grand final try
The pair tasted success together in 2018 and 2019 but there will be no love lost when they face off on Saturday night.
"I had 10 years working with Trent so it was a long apprenticeship," Fitzgibbon said. "I had plenty of lessons and I'm forever grateful for my time there and his mentoring of me as a coach.
"He was always supportive and backed me in to take the opportunity when it came. I'll be forever grateful for that but this week's about Sharks versus Roosters and while we talk regularly, we're not talking this week."

Robinson has long been viewed as one of the smartest and most respected coaches in the game. The former Tiger and Eel enjoyed instant success as a coach, first with Catalans before leading the Roosters to premiership glory in his first season in charge in 2013.
Throughout more than a decade, Robinson has mentored and helped develop a production line of assistants who have gone on to become head coaches.
Fitzgibbon headlines the list, along with current Eels coach Jason Ryles, former Knights coach Adam O'Brien and current Knights coach Justin Holbrook.
It's no coincidence both the Sharks and Newcastle are still alive in this year's competition.
Nicho calls on Sharks faithful to pack the stands
Current Roosters assistants Matt King and Michael Cheika are also in their final days with the club before taking on head coaching roles of the NSW Blues and NSW Waratahs, respectively.
While proud to see his former assistants flourish, Robinson said personal relationships will be put to the side this week as the Roosters put their season on the line.
"We honour the clubs we play for and coach for and that's our role," Robinson said. "All of [the relationships] get put aside.
"If that emotion creeps in, you're not built for the role. You go about your business, you're purely focused on what the Roosters need to do this week.
"We're a close group from a friendship point of view, there's a shared care for each other but it's footy, no one cares about that outside our personal relationships. It's about Saturday night, for Justin it's about Sunday.
"We've got roles to play. Our role is to go out there and coach our team, offer the best support we can to our players to go and nail the best game."
Fitzgibbon has enjoyed considerable success since leaving the Roosters to take charge of the Sharks in 2022.
Cronulla have played finals football in every year since he took over and are chasing a third-straight preliminary final this weekend.
The Sharks are riding high after an elimination final victory over the Cowboys, while the Roosters are desperate to rebound from last week's tight loss to Penrith.
Cronulla knocked the Roosters out of the competition last season but Robinson enjoyed some revenge this year, his side winning both matches played throughout the season.

NRL Late Mail: Finals Week 2 - Lucas in the mix; Crichton cleared
Newcastle star Dylan Lucas has until Saturday to prove his fitness for a sudden-death clash with the Warriors while Angus Crichton is set to return for the Roosters this weekend.
Lucas fractured his ankle in Round 21 and has been listed in the Knights' extended squad for this weekend's semi-final at a sold-out Eden Park in Auckland.
Talking to the media on Thursday afternoon, Newcastle coach Justin Holbrook said a final decision on Lucas' fitness will be made on Saturday.
"Everyone trained well, obviously Dyl Lucas is the one we will see how he pulls up and we won’t make a decision on him until Saturday," Holbrook told reporters.
"Credit to the medical staff and Dylan, the day he got injured he wanted to fast track himself and do everything right. If he gets there on Sunday we will all be happy for Dyl."
Roosters coach Trent Robinson has also declared Crichton will return from a long-term foot injury in Saturday's clash with the Sharks.
"He's ready to go," Robinson said on Friday.

'Taught me a lot': Hynes embracing blockbuster halves battle
A close friendship will be put to the side when star playmakers Nicho Hynes and Daly Cherry-Evans go head-to-head in Saturday night's blockbuster semi-final.
Two of the biggest names in the game, the battle of the halfbacks will go a long way to determining the winner of the sudden-death clash at Allianz Stadium.
A Sea Eagles junior, Hynes first crossed paths with Cherry-Evans more than a decade ago when he spent a summer training alongside the Manly senior squad.
Nicho in the tries
It wasn't until they were representative teammates that they formed a close bond, with Hynes crediting the Roosters halfback for helping him handle the pressure of life in the No.7 jumper.
"I spent one pre-season with him," Hynes said. "When you're going through the grades and you get to watch people, how they go about their business, they're mannerisms and the way they speak. That's what I learned the most.
"I didn't get to develop a great relationship at the time because I was so young and didn't get to experience too much with him. As I've gotten older and experienced an Aussie tour with him, I've got heaps closer to him.
"I've rung him for advice over the last couple of years. He's a great guy and I really valued my time with Chez in that Aussie camp and the Prime Minister's XIII we played in together.
"He's a great guy, been there and done it all before so he'll be coming out firing this week."

items.body_excerpt:
How injured star helped unleash Roosters young gun
Emerging forward Salesi Foketi has credited representative star Angus Crichton for mentoring him during a rapid rise from NRL debut to Roosters star.
Foketi has long been viewed as Crichton's long-term replacement when the veteran departs at the end of the season but a serious foot injury accelerated the succession plan.
The 20-year-old has looked at home on the Roosters left edge and delivered 53 exceptional minutes in his maiden finals appearance last weekend.
Salesi Foketi Try
While Crichton is expected to return from injury in Saturday's sudden-death clash with the Sharks, Foketi has retained his place in the starting side and will look to target Cronulla halfback Nicho Hynes throughout the match at Allianz Stadium.
"Seeing the way Gussy trains and the way he plays every time he takes the field is inspiring," Foketi told NRL.com.
"Being able to learn from him, seeing how he goes about it all and picking up tiny details from him is huge. It's helped me tremendously out there on the field."

Foketi grew up in Auckland before moving to Sydney as a 17-year-old to join the Roosters pathways program.
The edge forward quickly rose through the club's flourishing development pipeline before making his debut in Round 1 last season.
Foketi featured in 19 games in his rookie campaign and has quickly developed into a key figure in the Roosters pack.
In a sign of how important the youngster is to coach Trent Robinson, an ill Foketi was given every chance to prove his fitness for last week's clash with the Panthers.
The forward battled influenza all week leading into the game and was only cleared to take his place in the squad a few hours before kick-off.
While he remained in the squad, Foketi started the match on the six-man bench and was only expecting to feature late in the contest. That changed just 19 minutes into the game when Egan Butcher suffered a head knock, with Foketi thrust into the action much earlier than anticipated.
"I hadn't been with the boys since [Wednesday]," Foketi said. "I hadn't trained, barely ate and was in bed most of the time.
"I went in on the day of the game and Robbo asked how I was feeling. You put the boys first, they give you that bit of energy so I said I was good to go.
"It was an intense atmosphere but in some ways I was fortunate to be sick and not have all the build up around it being a finals game. Leading into this week there will be more hype."
Foketi will line up on the Roosters left edge on Saturday night, directly opposite Sharks, and Kiwis, forward Briton Nikora.
The match provides Foketi with a chance to prove he belongs in Stacy Jones' New Zealand squad for the upcoming World Cup, while he is also eligible for Tonga and was a member of Kristian Woolf's squad for last year's Pacific Championships.
The representative hype comes as no surprise to the youngster's Roosters teammates, who have been impressed with Foketi's ability to repeatedly elevate his game.
Radley ready for showdown in the middle
"Salesi's character is the most impressive thing," experienced lock Victor Radley said. "He puts his teammates first, you can tell in his effort areas and what he works on in his game.
"He's got some brilliant moments, when he folds blokes or steps someone or carries as powerfully as he does but his character and how he puts his teammates before anyone else is super impressive.
"[Last week] he could have easily said 'it's not for me today' just to cover his own backside but he said 'no, I want to turn up and give it my all'. We ended up needing him to play big minutes so it's super impressive."

Redemption mission driving Roosters into sudden-death showdown
The opportunity for a rematch with the Panthers is driving the Roosters in their bid to navigate two weeks of sudden-death football and book a spot in the NRL grand final.
The two teams played out an epic qualifying final last weekend, with Nathan Cleary slotting a 70th minute field goal to help send Penrith into the preliminary final.
The result has forced the Roosters into sudden-death football a week earlier than hoped and Trent Robinson's men will now take on Cronulla in a must-win semi-final at Allianz Stadium on Saturday night.
Panthers v Roosters – Finals Week 1, 2026
While disappointed not to come away with the result, the Roosters have taken plenty of confidence from their performance and set their sights on setting up a rematch with the Panthers on grand final day.
"We saw we're able to go toe-to-toe with the premiership favourites," centre Rob Toia said. "That was a big takeaway we can take from that game.
"Some of the boys on the Penrith team mentioned a few times 'we'll be seeing you in the GF'. I didn't think of it at the time but if we win our games the next two weeks we'll meet them in the grand final if both teams get through."

Trent Robinson's side pushed the minor premiers to the brink and could have prevailed had a couple of key moments swung in their favour.
Tedesco chats Panthers lessons and Sharks challenge
Lock Victor Radley revealed he was up at 3am on Monday pondering the chance that slipped through his side's grasp but has quickly turned his focus to Saturday's clash with the Sharks.
"I had that feeling [after Sunday] that I know where we stand," Radley said. "We're in a good spot and nothing's more important than this week.
"As disappointing as the weekend was, we know we're in a good place."
While the result didn't go their way, there were plenty of positives to take out of Sunday's game for the Roosters.
The Tricolours were superb in defence and largely contained Penrith's attacking weapons.
Mark Nawaqanitawase was immense for the Roosters
There were also promising signs from Daly Cherry-Evans' halves partnership with Hugo Savala, with the pair to link up again this weekend as Sam Walker continues his recovery from an ankle injury.
While Cronulla will pose a different challenge on Saturday night, Roosters captain James Tedesco is confident his side can finish on top.
"Our performance was really good," Tedesco said. "I didn't think we got outplayed, our physicality was really good and our defence on the goal line was awesome.
Radley ready for showdown in the middle
"You look at those positives and there's a couple of moments we want to clear up and fix this weekend but it's about bringing positivity into this week. Especially with the young crew we've got, we're not getting down on ourselves.
"We know the areas we want to improve on and focus on in our sessions this week so we're ready to go on Saturday night."

NRL Match Preview: Week 2 Finals v Roosters
The Sharks take some finals momentum into their semi-final against the Roosters at Allianz Stadium tomorrow night.
After a tough end to the regular season, a 26-16 win over the Cowboys has Cronulla cracking the whips at the right time.
Especially with Braydon Trindall's shoulder tried and tested and all the better for the hit-out.
"His shoulder pulled up really good to be honest," coach Craig Fitzgibbon shared.
"A couple of little stingers there which sort of shocked it, but it's really stable, and his strength's really good at the moment, so I think he'll be better for it.
"Obviously it was about a month on the sidelines there and he worked really hard in that. The performance staff didn't miss him to make sure he was ready to come back in."
Fans won't want to miss Ronaldo Mulitalo versus Mark Nawaqanitawase either.
One of the most anticipated winger duels in recent memory.
"Ronnie really respects Mark, and I think you would have seen it after the last game and Ronnie knows that the discipline in a semi-final is crucial," Fitzgibbon said.
"So, he'll be playing for his team in the way Ronnie does and with a respect for his opponent, but it's great to have two of the better wingers in the competition going at it, but no, it'll be focused on the game of football rather than any theatrics."
The battle off the field has been intense too. Sharks' fans HAD purchased the majority of Saturday's tickets as of Thursday night, before the Roosters faithful took the lead in what is their home final.
"We feel the support immensely in the Shire and yeah having them out there to know they'll be vocal for us is definitely an asset, but we want to perform for them as well," the Cronulla coach added.
Fitzgibbon is the first coach in the Sharks history to lead the club to five straight finals appearances.
The Roosters have won 3/4 of the final's clashes between both clubs, but Cronulla broke the drought in last year's week 1 elimination final with a 20-10 win over the tri-colours at Ocean Protect Stadium.
The Sharks have won four of their past six Finals games, with preliminary final losses to Penrith (2024) and Melbourne (2025).
Cronulla receives the fewest penalties and concedes the third-most and records the second-most ruck infringements.
Braydon Trindall (31) and Nicho Hynes (23) have the most try-assists by a halves combination in recent memory.
Briton Nikora is chasing his 100th NRL win and Addin Fonua-Blake will play his 50th NRL game for the Sharks in tomorrow's semi-final against the Roosters.

Eight teams are now reduced to six and with two resting this weekend, four teams will take centre stage in Week 2 of the NRL Finals series . Following an exhilarating start, the intensity is expected to lift to another level, with action beginning on Saturday as the Roosters host the Sharks . Facing elimination with a loss, neither team will want to end their season with a poor performance here. Two quality teams face off and bring different form lines into this contest. Before You Bet is here to help with a comprehensive look at what is ahead in this match.
Roosters vs Sharks Prediction & Tips: 2026 NRL Semi Final
Roosters Brave in defeat
Few gave the Roosters a chance of competing with the Panthers last week, but they were gallant in their 19-12 defeat. In a gruelling match, the Roosters overcame a 45% share of possession and 73% completion rate to push their opponents over 80 minutes. This saw them make 8.7m per carry and 5 line breaks, continually taking their chances but failing to close out the last part of the match. What went wrong for them was a lack of execution in key moments rather than missing opportunities; they had their chances to build pressure when it mattered. Providing they can recover quickly; they should take confidence from how they performed in that match.
Sharks Back on track
In a confidence building victory, the Sharks defeated the Cowboys 26-16 in an elimination match. The improved performance coincided with the return of Trindall in the halves, changing their attacking structure and giving others confidence. Commanding possession (54%), they had a superior completion rate (82%), made 9.2m per carry, and 618 PCM’s. Continually creating second phase play, they made 5 line breaks also, pressuring their opponents in the middle and striking on the edges. The performance of several key players in the spine was also impressive to watch and should serve them well moving forward.
Stats that matter
- These two sides have met twice this year, with the Roosters prevailing on both occasions. They won the Round 16 meeting 27-8 at this ground, while they captured victory in Perth during Round 6 34-22.
- The Roosters have a 64% record at this ground compared to the Sharks 49%. Interestingly, the home side has won 7 out of the past 10 matches between these two sides.
- In the past 5 matches between these two sides, only 2 have been decided by fewer that 12 points, with the average margin of victory being 16 points. They have been relatively low-scoring affairs, with the average sitting at 45.6 total points with 2 games under 35 total points.
- The Sharks have a great attack this year, averaging 27ppg compared to the Roosters 25ppg. The difference in their defence isn’t much either. The Roosters have the edge though, allowing 20ppg ahead of the Sharks 21ppg.
Fatigue to be a deciding factor
The Roosters are coming off a bruising contest against the Panthers and have a short turnaround heading into this match. This gives a Sharks a chance to perform well but in equal measure, the Roosters are a professional organisation capable of managing it. For the Sharks to win, they must set a relentless intensity throughout this match. It starts with their forwards, hopefully giving the outside backs extra space. Like the earlier point, the Roosters are strong defensively on the edge and will be prepared for this.
